tools: Figma Design + Figma MCP agent; existing code and finance-engine output
log: We began with an existing LedgerLens build and a team report that earlier Figma files were lost. We reconstructed the idea around one inspectable claim: a duplicate supplier payment. Figma Design made the input, evidence, proposed action, and owner decision visible together. The money tree stayed because its roots and branches map to real records and findings. Output: a four-state evidence-to-action flow and a consistent paper, blue, and orange visual language. This log describes the current reconstruction session; historical Figma files and timings are not available.

We built native editable Discover, Prove, Prepare, and Review screens, with five prototype actions, auto layout, semantic variables, shared text styles, and a reusable primary button. The tree artwork comes from the existing procedural generator. Screenshot review exposed clipped receipt cards and wrapped button labels; both were corrected before handoff. The flow makes identified opportunity distinct from recovered cash and labels demo approval as local only. Output: a clickable Figma prototype that carries the same invoice, amount, evidence, and approval boundary through every state.

tools: Figma Design variables + Figma MCP agent
log: We read the semantic variables back from Figma and exported them to design-tokens.json. Those exact values generated the runnable prototype’s tokens.css. Layout and state behavior were kept in readable source files beside the exported tokens. The finance-engine export supplies the monetary figures and the procedural tree supplies the artwork, so design and code share more than screenshots. Output: traceable Figma-to-CSS color tokens, linked prototype states, source-derived data and artwork, and a small implementation with explicit approval and reset behavior.

tools: Codex for implementation; Figma Design for the handoff; Figma Make import attempted
log: Codex produced a responsive HTML/CSS/JavaScript Evidence Lab from the Figma flow and exported tokens. We checked the engine-derived totals, approval gate, repeated approval, and reset, and checked JavaScript syntax. Figma Make was chosen to host a runnable version beside the design, but the environment’s network blocked the source upload before import. We retained the local runnable source and the working native Figma prototype. Make preview and browser playback are not claimed as verified. Output: packaged implementation plus the existing public full-product repository and demo.
